comment: Regression budgets for `cua-bench-streaming check`. Each entry: glob `match` over run ids (runtime/transport/decoder/client/scenario), a metric, and max and/or min. Thresholds are loose enough for a 4-vCPU hosted runner with software (OpenH264) encode and decode; tighten them on dedicated or GPU runners. `optional` entries do not fail when the run or metric is missing (lanes that depend on toolchains).

budgets.note: plan §8.5 budget ±40 ms (runc; VMs and hosts use the same)

gVisor (runsc) exception, measured 2026-09-22: the avsync fixture writes its beep with pacat (--latency-msec=20) and draws the flash at the same instant; in-container parec onset detection shows the beep reaching the sink monitor 40-53 ms after the write under runsc vs 18-42 ms under runc (pipewire-pulse IPC and timers run through the gVisor Sentry), while the flash is drawn within 1 ms in both. The capture side is not the cause: monitor delivery jitter is the same in both runtimes (p50 4-7 ms, rate within 0.2% of real time). So the skew is the fixture content's own playback latency, which does not fit ±40 under runsc; the driver reports it as an audio.desktop limitation under gVisor.
